name: tell-me
description: Habit tracker built around one question: did you show up? Yes/No check-ins and weekly insights. Web app + iPhone app.

paragraphs: A habit tracker built around one question: did you show up?
Write your schedule in plain English. When it's time, your phone asks Yes or No.
Every week you get a report that shows what's working and what isn't.
features: Plain-English quick add. Gym Mon Wed Fri 6pm, French class Tue/Thu 19h30, Read daily 22:00, Run 3x a week. You can also paste or import a whole schedule (text, CSV or a backup file).

Native iPhone app. The same app in a native shell (Capacitor). Reminders are scheduled on the phone itself with ✅ Yes / ❌ No buttons right on the notification, with no server at all. Share it through TestFlight or the…

Yes/No push reminders on the web. On Android and desktop Chrome/Edge you answer straight from the notification, without opening the app. On iPhone (Home Screen web app, iOS 16.4+) and Safari you tap the notification to…

Stronger reminders. Per habit: if a check-in is still unanswered 30 minutes later, it asks again, and on computers the notification stays on screen until you answer. Answering on any device cancels the second ask.

Water check-ins for everyone. Every user starts with three water check-ins that add up to 4 litres a day (1 L in the morning, 1.5 L at noon, 1.5 L in the evening), with stronger reminders. They're ordinary habits:…

requirements.text: Without an account, everything stays on your device (IndexedDB).

The friends test drives three real browsers against the real worker: two people sign up, connect through an invite link, check in, react, nudge and run a challenge, and the first person's laptop signs in with the account key and syncs everything, with changes showing up live on the other device.
